title: Old Malta Overview
subtitle: Listen to the lesson explained in English

transcript.en: Welcome! 👋 Unit 12: Old Malta.
Today we go back in time. The shops your grandparents used, the way people got around before cars, and the one small word that lets you talk about all of it. Let's go!
🪡 PART 1: OLD SHOPS 🪡
Every village had these, and most of the trades have gone. The words have not. The barber:
the baker:
and the blacksmith:
Then the shops themselves, and they are all built the same way. The word for shop, then what it sells. The grocery shop:
and the sweet shop:
Learn the pattern rather than the list. Shop, then of-the, then the thing. Once you have it, you can build a shop for almost anything. 💡
🚇 PART 2: GETTING AROUND 🚇
Long before buses there was a mule and two wooden wheels:
Later came the covered carriage you still see in Valletta:
Malta really did have a railway, from Valletta up to Mdina, and a tram as well. The railway:
and the tram:
Both closed in the nineteen thirties. What you use today is the bus:
and, out on the water, the Gozo ferry:
🗣️ PART 3: TALKING TO YOUR GRANDFATHER 🗣️
Mary asks her grandfather how he got to work. Listen for one word turning up in almost every line:

transcript.mt: Nannu, kif kont tmur għax-xogħol meta kont żgħir?

transcript.en: He used to go by tram, or by bus:

transcript.mt: Kont immur bit-tramm jew bil-karozza tal-linja.

transcript.en: And what did he do for a living?
⏳ PART 4: KONT ⏳
That word is the past of the verb to be, and it takes exactly the endings you already know from other verbs. I was:
he was:
she was:
and they were:
Now the useful part. Put kont in front of another verb and you get 'used to'. Kont immur is I used to go. Kont niekol is I used to eat. Put it in front of a noun instead and it simply means 'was'. 💡
One last thing, carried over from last unit. A shop is ħanut, and shops are:
The word rebuilt itself from the inside rather than taking an ending. That is a broken plural, and you met the same machinery in Unit 11. 💡
📖 PART 5: USING KONT 📖
Three tools to finish with. First, to say you were not something, wrap kont the way you wrap any verb, ma in front and x on the end. I did not work as a blacksmith:
Second, there was and there were. Maltese uses one phrase for both, and it does not change for the plural. There were many shops in Valletta:

transcript.mt: Kien hemm ħafna ħwienet il-Belt Valletta

transcript.en: Watch the capital letter there. With a small b, fil-belt means in the city, any city at all. With a capital B, il-Belt is Valletta itself, and it takes no preposition. 💡
And third, put a question word in front of kont and you can ask anyone about their own past. Where did you work?
🎉 THAT'S UNIT 12 🎉
Old shops, old ways of getting around, and the past tense to talk about all of it. Tap a card to flip it, use Play all to hear a whole section hands-free, and try the exercises. Prosit, well done!
